_about: Text specs the curated corner cases were written from. Each pairs a plain-language description of the hazard with construction notes: map, weather, traffic side, and Scenic patterns already verified in CARLA (lane filters, spawn geometry, behaviour idioms). The .scenic file with the same id implements the spec.

scenarios.description: The ego vehicle is driving at 50 km/h along a straight, undivided two-lane road with one lane in each direction, in clear daylight. A sedan is approaching head-on inside the ego vehicle's own lane, driving the wrong way against traffic in a perfectly straight line at a constant 40 km/h, without weaving or correcting its course. The ego vehicle must recognise the oncoming vehicle in its own lane and brake or steer around it.
scenarios.construction_notes:
STRAIGHTNESS AND LANE SELECTION ARE MANDATORY. Use exactly this filter (verified
to sample on this map -- do not invent a different one):

    import math
    laneSecs = []
    for lane in network.lanes:
        for laneSec in lane.sections:
            pts = laneSec.centerline.points
            if len(pts) < 2 or laneSec.centerline.length <= 40:
                continue
            straightness = math.dist(tuple(pts[0])[:2], tuple(pts[-1])[:2]) / laneSec.centerline.length
            if straightness > 0.97 and len(laneSec.lane.road.lanes) == 2 and laneSec._laneToLeft is not None and laneSec._laneToLeft.isForward != laneSec.isForward:
                laneSecs.append(laneSec)
    egoLaneSec = Uniform(*laneSecs)
    egoSpawnPt = new OrientedPoint in egoLaneSec.centerline

This yields a straight, undivided TWO-LANE road: one lane each way, no extra lanes.
Verified section counts: Town01 34, Town02 18, Town03 12, Town04 12, Town05 0.
NEVER pick a map with 0.

THE WRONG-WAY / OPPOSING ACTOR MUST NOT USE FollowLaneBehavior OR LaneChangeBehavior.
Reason (verified in the Scenic source): `is_oppositeTraffic` only flips the sign of
the lateral PID's cross-track error; the behavior still walks the lane centerline in
its NOMINAL direction, so a vehicle driving backwards along it steers toward
waypoints that are behind it and the PID hunts -- the car visibly weaves left and
right. Drive it with plain throttle and an explicitly zeroed steer instead:

    behavior WrongWayBehavior(throttle):
        while True:
            take SetThrottleAction(throttle), SetSteerAction(0.0)

Spawn it with `following roadDirection from egoSpawnPt for <dist>` and
`facing <pt>.heading + 180 deg`. On a straight section this gives a clean,
dead-straight head-on with no weaving.

EXACTLY TWO VEHICLES in the scene: the ego and the wrong-way sedan. No other traffic.
Spawn the sedan `following roadDirection from egoSpawnPt for Range(30, 40)`.
Give it throttle Range(0.45, 0.55).

            pts = laneSec.centerline.points
            if len(pts) < 2 or laneSec.centerline.length <= 120:
                continue

            if straightness > 0.97 and len(laneSec.lane.road.lanes) == 2 \
               and laneSec._laneToLeft is not None \

    egoLaneSec = Uniform(*laneSecs)

Measured straight two-lane two-way sections: Town01 34 (longest 309 m), Town02 18
(longest 177 m), Town03 12, Town04 12, Town05 0, Town10HD 2. Never use Town05 for
a two-lane scenario.

LEFT-HAND TRAFFIC. The source dash-cam clip is from a left-hand-drive country, so
the ego and the hazard are both in the lane that is visually on the LEFT. CARLA's
maps are right-hand-drive, so build the left-hand layout explicitly. Anchor
everything to a point in the map's nominal forward lane, then put the EGO one lane
width to its left, still facing forward:

    egoBase = new OrientedPoint at egoLaneSec.centerline.pointAlongBy(6), facing roadDirection
    egoSpawnPt = new OrientedPoint left of egoBase by 3.5, facing egoBase.heading

That places the ego in the opposing lane of the map, which renders exactly as
left-hand traffic: centre line on the ego's right, kerb on its left. Then:
  - anything in the EGO'S OWN lane is `left of <basePt> by 3.5`
  - anything in the lane to the EGO'S RIGHT (oncoming traffic) has NO lateral
    offset - it sits on <basePt> itself
where `basePt = new OrientedPoint following roadDirection from egoBase for <d>`.
A vehicle coming head-on at the ego faces `<basePt>.heading + 180 deg`.

IMPORTANT: because the ego is in the map's opposing lane, any behavior that has to
aim at the EGO'S lane centreline must use `egoLaneSec._laneToLeft.centerline`,
NOT `egoLaneSec.centerline`.

NEVER drive a wrong-way / opposing actor with FollowLaneBehavior or
LaneChangeBehavior, even with is_oppositeTraffic=True. That flag only flips the
sign of the lateral PID's cross-track error while the behavior still walks the
lane centreline forwards, so the actor steers at waypoints behind itself and the
PID hunts - it visibly weaves. Drive it dead straight instead:

    behavior WrongWayBehavior(throttle):
        while True:
            take SetThrottleAction(throttle), SetSteerAction(0.0)

EXACTLY TWO VEHICLES. The wrong-way sedan sits in the EGO'S OWN lane:
    advBase = new OrientedPoint following roadDirection from egoBase for Range(28, 34)
    advPt = new OrientedPoint left of advBase by 3.5, facing advBase.heading + 180 deg
with throttle Range(0.80, 0.90).

scenarios.description: The ego vehicle is driving at 30 km/h in the left-hand lane of an urban arterial and has just cleared a signalised intersection. A queue of six cars is stopped in the lane to the ego vehicle's right, waiting at the light. A motorcycle at the head of that queue pulls out from behind the stopped cars, crosses the centre line into the ego vehicle's left-hand lane, and rides the wrong way straight toward the ego vehicle.
scenarios.construction_notes:
Lane filter: a straight two-lane two-way section that is an OUTGOING lane of a
SIGNALISED intersection and at least 120 m long, so the whole queue fits past the
junction. Verified: Town01's signalised exits run to 224 m; Town03's 4-way exits
are only 42-52 m and push the rear of the queue into the next junction.

    import math
    laneSecs = []
    for intersection in network.intersections:
        if not intersection.isSignalized:
            continue
        for lane in intersection.outgoingLanes:
            for laneSec in lane.sections:
                pts = laneSec.centerline.points
                if len(pts) < 2 or laneSec.centerline.length <= 120:
                    continue
                straightness = math.dist(tuple(pts[0])[:2], tuple(pts[-1])[:2]) / laneSec.centerline.length
                if straightness > 0.97 and len(laneSec.lane.road.lanes) == 2 \
                   and laneSec._laneToLeft is not None \
                   and laneSec._laneToLeft.isForward != laneSec.isForward:
                    laneSecs.append(laneSec)
    egoLaneSec = Uniform(*laneSecs)

left-hand lane and stays there.

CRITICAL - the truck previously drove onto the pavement because the crossing was
open-loop. It must stop crossing as soon as it reaches the EGO'S lane centreline,
and because the ego is in the map's opposing lane that centreline is
`egoLaneSec._laneToLeft.centerline`:

    behavior PullOutBehavior(throttle, trigger, steer):
        for i in range(60):
            if (distance from self to ego) < trigger:
                break
            take SetThrottleAction(throttle), SetSteerAction(0.0)
        for i in range(60):
            if egoLaneSec._laneToLeft.centerline.distanceTo(self.position) < 1.0:
                break
            take SetThrottleAction(throttle), SetSteerAction(steer)
        for i in range(12):
            take SetThrottleAction(throttle), SetSteerAction(-steer)
        while True:
            take SetThrottleAction(throttle), SetSteerAction(0.0)

ego's lane is on the truck's RIGHT here (the ego is to the LEFT of the map's
forward lane, and the truck faces backwards along it) - verify against the trace
and flip if the truck moves away.

scenarios.description: The ego vehicle is driving at 70 km/h in the left-hand lane of a multi-lane divided highway, immediately beside the centre line. A pickup truck crosses from the far side of the road, perpendicular to the flow of traffic, and noses into the ego vehicle's lane while still accelerating from a standstill.
scenarios.construction_notes:
THIS CLIP IS FROM A RIGHT-HAND-DRIVE COUNTRY (United States) - do NOT apply the
left-hand-traffic construction. The ego is in the LEFT-HAND lane of its own
carriageway, i.e. the leftmost lane, with the opposing traffic across a painted
centre line to its left:

    import math
    laneSecs = []
    for lane in network.lanes:
        for laneSec in lane.sections:
            pts = laneSec.centerline.points
            if len(pts) < 2 or laneSec.centerline.length <= 60:
                continue
            straightness = math.dist(tuple(pts[0])[:2], tuple(pts[-1])[:2]) / laneSec.centerline.length
            if straightness > 0.97 \
               and laneSec._laneToLeft is not None \
               and laneSec._laneToLeft.isForward != laneSec.isForward \
               and laneSec._laneToRight is not None \
               and laneSec._laneToRight.isForward == laneSec.isForward:
                laneSecs.append(laneSec)

Town04's leftmost lane sits against a Jersey barrier: a vehicle placed on the
median there has its tail inside the barrier mesh and physics ejects it randomly.
Town05 has leftmost lanes separated from opposing traffic by a painted line.

THE PICKUP starts in the opposing lane 3.5 m to the left, angled 70 deg across the
road, and crosses into the ego's lane and stops there.

The runner ticks NUM_HISTORY=16 warmup frames before frame 0. An adversary that
starts moving immediately has already covered ground before the episode begins.
Trigger dynamic adversaries on the EGO'S DISTANCE with a bounded timeout loop, so
the hazard neither fires during warmup nor deadlocks if the ego stops short:

    for i in range(50):
        if (distance from self to ego) < TRIGGER:
            break
        take SetBrakeAction(1.0)

CARLA's VehicleControl is PERSISTENT and each Set*Action mutates one field, so a
SetBrakeAction(1.0) stays applied until cleared. Any throttle after a braking or
waiting phase MUST clear the brake in the same tick:
    take SetThrottleAction(t), SetBrakeAction(0.0), SetSteerAction(0.0)

scenarios.description: The ego vehicle is approaching a signalised crossing at 40 km/h at night on a green light when a pedestrian steps off the kerb and walks straight across the ego vehicle's lane against the signal.             straightness = math.dist(tuple(pts[0])[:2], tuple(pts[-1])[:2]) / laneSec.centerline.length
            if straightness > 0.97 and len(laneSec.lane.road.lanes) == 2 \
               and laneSec._laneToLeft is not None \
               and laneSec._laneToLeft.isForward != laneSec.isForward:
                laneSecs.append(laneSec)
    egoLaneSec = Uniform(*laneSecs)

THE PEDESTRIAN starts on the kerb to the ego's RIGHT and walks across the lane.
Place it with a lateral offset from a point ahead in the ego's own lane and drive
it with a constant walking speed toward the far side:

    pedBase = new OrientedPoint following roadDirection from egoSpawnPt for Range(22, 28)
    pedPt = new OrientedPoint right of pedBase by 4.5, facing pedBase.heading + 90 deg
    behavior CrossBehavior(speed):
        for i in range(50):
            if (distance from self to ego) < 20:
                break
            wait
        while True:
            take SetWalkingSpeedAction(speed)
    walker = new Pedestrian at pedPt, with heading pedBase.heading + 90 deg,
        with behavior CrossBehavior(1.6)

The pedestrian must be triggered by the ego's distance so the crossing happens
during the episode rather than during the 16-tick warmup. Exactly one non-ego object.

LEFT-HAND TRAFFIC. The source dash-cam clip is from a left-hand-drive country, so
the ego and the hazard are both in the lane that is visually on the LEFT. CARLA's
maps are right-hand-drive, so build the left-hand layout explicitly. Anchor
everything to a point in the map's nominal forward lane, then put the EGO one lane
width to its left, still facing forward:

    egoBase = new OrientedPoint at egoLaneSec.centerline.pointAlongBy(6), facing roadDirection
    egoSpawnPt = new OrientedPoint left of egoBase by 3.5, facing egoBase.heading

That places the ego in the opposing lane of the map, which renders exactly as
left-hand traffic: centre line on the ego's right, kerb on its left. Then:
  - anything in the EGO'S OWN lane is `left of <basePt> by 3.5`
  - anything in the lane to the EGO'S RIGHT (oncoming traffic) has NO lateral
    offset - it sits on <basePt> itself
where `basePt = new OrientedPoint following roadDirection from egoBase for <d>`.
A vehicle coming head-on at the ego faces `<basePt>.heading + 180 deg`.

IMPORTANT: because the ego is in the map's opposing lane, any behavior that has to
aim at the EGO'S lane centreline must use `egoLaneSec._laneToLeft.centerline`,
NOT `egoLaneSec.centerline`.

THE PEDESTRIAN starts on the near-side kerb, which for the ego in the LEFT-hand
lane is to the ego's LEFT, and walks across the ego's lane:

    pedBase = new OrientedPoint following roadDirection from egoBase for Range(22, 28)
    pedAnchor = new OrientedPoint left of pedBase by 3.5
    pedPt = new OrientedPoint left of pedAnchor by 4.0, facing pedAnchor.heading - 90 deg

Trigger the walk on the ego's distance (< 18 m) with a bounded timeout so it does
not happen during the 16-tick warmup, then walk at 1.6 m/s. Exactly one non-ego object.

CARLA's VehicleControl is PERSISTENT and each Set*Action mutates one field, so a
SetBrakeAction(1.0) stays applied until cleared. Any throttle after a braking or
waiting phase MUST clear the brake in the same tick:
    take SetThrottleAction(t), SetBrakeAction(0.0), SetSteerAction(0.0)
